finding.claim: Unauthenticated /rss route passes attacker-controlled params[:u] directly to URI.open, which fetches arbitrary http(s) URLs server-side with no validation, and returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the caller (non-blind SSRF).
finding.guards_checked: None on the path: no scheme restriction, no host or IP allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local block, no port restriction, no redirect limit (open-uri follows redirects).

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:7-9 has no scheme, host, IP, port, or redirect checks between params[:u] and URI.open, and the response goes straight back via data[0, 400]. The only other file in the directory is app.rb, so there is no auth middleware or helper in scope. Lines 12-14 (/trusted) have an exact-host allowlist, but that is a different route and does not guard /rss.
verdict.reason: The /rss route at app.rb:7 passes attacker-controlled params[:u] unchanged into URI.open at app.rb:8 and returns the first 400 bytes of the fetched body at app.rb:9, with no closing guard on that path. "Unauthenticated" rests on the absence of any auth code in the only file present, not on a verified deployment setting.

finding.claim: /trusted enforces an exact-match host allowlist, but does not restrict port or scheme, so an attacker can choose any port on feeds.example.net or news.example.net and read the full response body. Likely low impact unless those hosts resolve to internal infrastructure or their DNS is attacker-controllable.

trace.note: halt 400 unless TRUSTED.include?(uri.host); TRUSTED defined at app.rb:5
Net::HTTP.get(uri) fetches the URL and returns the body

finding.guards_checked: Exact string match on uri.host against TRUSTED (fails closed for case and trailing-dot variants). Userinfo tricks do not bypass the check. Net::HTTP.get does not follow redirects. Not validated: port and scheme.

verdict.guard_found: app.rb:14 `halt 400, "no" unless TRUSTED.include?(uri.host)`, an exact set-membership check on the parsed hostname against the frozen TRUSTED list at app.rb:5 (feeds.example.net, news.example.net).
verdict.reason: All four trace lines (app.rb:12-15) match the candidate's description and params[:u] is attacker-controlled, but app.rb:14 is exact hostname set membership on uri.host, which closes the finding under the stated criteria; the unrestricted port and scheme the candidate notes are not a closing-guard requirement, so the residual exposure is low-impact and not the SSRF the finding describes.
